user_query: We are planning a Phase 3 randomised controlled trial of a next-generation proteasome inhibitor in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, targeting patients with 2–3 prior lines of therapy including lenalidomide and a prior PI. The trial will be conducted globally across the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. We are seeking FDA and EMA label claims and will need NICE and ICER submissions. The mechanism involves weekly IV administration with step-up dosing in Cycle 1. Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.
assumptions_made: EUnetHTA and SMC not mentioned; only NICE and ICER extracted from explicit text
answer:
## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** Capture the patient-reported impact of bone pain, physical function, and fatigue changes with a proteasome inhibitor in RRMM patients while meeting FDA/EMA labelling requirements and HTA utility needs.

**Key challenge:** FDA requires core PRO domains but no KG comparator trials exist for this indication, necessitating reliance on published validation data and expert judgment rather than drug class-specific precedent.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 for comprehensive coverage validated in MM, MDASI-MM for symptom burden sensitivity, EQ-5D-5L for NICE/ICER requirements.

**Critical gap:** No KG comparator data means endpoint positioning and SAP language precedent must be established independently — likely requiring secondary endpoint positioning for PRO claims.

## Table 1: Domain Coverage Comparison

| Concept | Key Stakeholder | Current Trial Candidates | No KG Comparator Data Available |
|---|---|---|---|
| Disease-related bone pain | FDA 2020 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-MY20 Disease Symptoms subscale — MDASI-MM bone aches item | No KG data for this indication |
| Physical function | FDA 2020 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-C30 Physical Functioning scale — MDASI-MM interference items | No KG data for this indication |
| Fatigue | FDA 2020 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-C30 Fatigue scale — MDASI-MM fatigue item | No KG data for this indication |
| Symptomatic adverse events | FDA 2020 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-MY20 Side Effects scale — MDASI-MM symptom items | No KG data for this indication |
| Side effect impact | FDA 2020 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-C30 symptom scales — MDASI-MM interference items | No KG data for this indication |
| Role function | FDA 2020 Core PRO Guidance | EORTC QLQ-C30 Role Functioning scales | No KG data for this indication |
| HTA utility | NICE — ICER requirements | EQ-5D-5L | No KG data for this indication |

## Table 2: PRO Measures Comparison

| Trial | Year | Drug | Drug class | PRO Measures (n items) | Assessment Schedule | Total items | Est. time (min) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Current Trial (Proposed) | 2026 | Next-generation PI | Proteasome Inhibitor | EORTC QLQ-C30 (30) — EORTC QLQ-MY20 (20) — MDASI-MM (26) — EQ-5D-5L (5) | TBD — expert decision required | 81 | 25 |

## Table 3: Instrument Gap Analysis

| Instrument | Content Validity | Psychometric Properties (FDA 3) | MCID Evidence | Regulatory Acceptance | Known Gaps / Risks | Fit for Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 | Validated in cancer patients including MM | α > 0.70 for all scales except cognitive functioning | 10-point change for global health status/physical functioning | Accepted FDA/EMA — multiple oncology indications | Limited disease-specific content for MM symptoms | Likely fit — validated in RRMM populations |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 | MM-specific module developed with patient input and clinical expert review | Good item convergence (72%) and discrimination (58%) | Not established — verify via PROQOLID | Accepted EMA — multiple MM submissions | Module developed in 1996 may not reflect current treatment landscape | Conditionally fit — requires MCID establishment for thresholds |
| MDASI-MM | MM-specific symptom inventory validated in RRMM patients | Cronbach α > 0.70 for all subscales | 2-point change for symptom severity — 1.5-point change for interference | No KG precedent | Limited regulatory precedent in Phase 3 settings | Likely fit — strong sensitivity to symptom changes in MM |
| EQ-5D-5L | Generic utility measure | Test-retest reliability > 0.80 | 0.074 utility difference | Accepted NICE/ICER — HTA standard | May lack sensitivity to MM-specific symptoms | Likely fit — required for NICE/ICER submissions |

## Table 4: Endpoint Positioning

No KG PRO endpoint SAP language precedent available for proteasome inhibitor trials in RRMM. Expert must establish positioning hierarchy independently.

## Table 5: Language & Translation Readiness

| Instrument | Validated Translations (approx.) | Key Languages Covered | Gap / Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC QLQ-C30 | 100+ | Spanish — French — German — Japanese — Mandarin — Portuguese | No action needed |
| EORTC QLQ-MY20 | 50+ | Major EU languages — some Asian languages | Verify Asia-Pacific coverage via PROQOLID |
| MDASI-MM | 15+ | English — Spanish — some European languages | Commission additional Asian translations — 6-9 months lead time |
| EQ-5D-5L | 200+ | All major global languages | No action needed |

## Key Observations

• **FDA core domains alignment:** [MDPI Guidelines](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/15/24/5764) confirms "core PROs, namely disease-related symptoms, symptomatic adverse events, overall side effect impact summary measure, physical function and role function" as essential for MM trials [1-21], directly supporting the domain coverage in Table 1.

• **Instrument selection precedent:** [PMC systematic review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10741926/) shows "EORTC QLQ-C30 was the most frequently used instrument (92 studies)" with "QLQ-MY20 MM-specific questionnaire was the second most frequently used (50 studies)" [6-11,6-12], validating Table 3 primary instrument choices.

• **MDASI-MM sensitivity evidence:** [Journal of Hematology validation](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1756-8722-6-13) demonstrates "excellent correlations with subscales of the 2 EORTC instruments, strong ability to distinguish clinically different patient groups" [12-12], supporting Table 3 fit-for-purpose assessment.

• **Missing regulatory precedent:** [Nature review](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41408-021-00543-y) notes "PRO information is frequently collected in registrational clinical trials, this information rarely is included in the USPI" [3-21], explaining the absence of Table 4 SAP language examples and indicating challenging regulatory pathway.

• **EMA multiplicity requirements:** KG regulatory rules [RULE-001] and [RULE-005] mandate "clear hypothesis-led strategy with measures selected based on scientific rationale" and "extensive advance planning with justification of unbiased instrument selection" for open-label designs [RULE-001,RULE-005], critical for Table 4 endpoint hierarchy planning.

• **HTA utility requirement:** Table 5 EQ-5D coverage is essential as "NICE requires a preference-based EQ-5D measure for cost-utility analysis" without which "UK reimbursement is severely compromised," making this a non-negotiable component despite limited MM sensitivity.

## Comparator Analysis

No COMP-XXX entries exist in the KG for this indication — expert should review recent FDA and EMA medical reviews for proteasome inhibitor submissions to identify instrument sensitivity and null result patterns.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In Candidate List? | Action Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Ensure baseline and key timepoints covered |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include in cost-effectiveness modeling plan |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. Primary versus secondary endpoint positioning for PRO measures given absence of precedent and likely requirement for hierarchical testing behind PFS/OS.
2. Whether to include all four candidate instruments or prioritize EORTC QLQ-C30/MY20 combination for regulatory focus with MDASI-MM as exploratory.
3. MCID thresholds for QLQ-MY20 since published values are not established — requires anchor-based validation or literature-derived estimates.
4. Assessment schedule aligned with weekly IV dosing and step-up tolerability monitoring in Cycle 1 versus standard 3-cycle oncology intervals.
5. Alpha control strategy for multiple PRO domains given EMA requirements for hypothesis-led design and FDA core domain expectations.
